us-presidents.name: George Washington
us-presidents.entry: Elected the first president under the Constitution.
us-presidents.fact: Presided over the Constitutional Convention before becoming president.

us-presidents.name: John Adams
us-presidents.entry: Won the 1796 presidential election after serving as vice president.
us-presidents.fact: The first president to live in the White House.

us-presidents.name: Thomas Jefferson
us-presidents.entry: Chosen by the House after the tied 1800 electoral vote.
us-presidents.fact: The Louisiana Purchase took place during his presidency.

us-presidents.name: James Madison
us-presidents.fact: President during the War of 1812.

us-presidents.name: James Monroe
us-presidents.fact: The Monroe Doctrine was announced during his presidency.

us-presidents.name: John Quincy Adams
us-presidents.entry: Chosen by the House after no candidate won an electoral majority in 1824.
us-presidents.fact: He later served in the U.S. House of Representatives.

us-presidents.name: Andrew Jackson
us-presidents.fact: His presidency included the Indian Removal Act and the forced displacement of Native peoples.

us-presidents.name: Martin Van Buren
us-presidents.fact: The first president born after the Declaration of Independence.

us-presidents.name: William Henry Harrison
us-presidents.fact: Died about a month after taking office, the shortest presidency.

us-presidents.name: John Tyler
us-presidents.entry: Succeeded William Henry Harrison after his death.
us-presidents.fact: Established the precedent that a vice president succeeds fully to the presidency.

us-presidents.name: James K. Polk
us-presidents.fact: President during the Mexican-American War.

us-presidents.name: Zachary Taylor
us-presidents.fact: A career army officer who died during his presidency.

us-presidents.name: Millard Fillmore
us-presidents.entry: Succeeded Zachary Taylor after his death.
us-presidents.fact: Signed measures in the Compromise of 1850, including California's admission.

us-presidents.name: Franklin Pierce
us-presidents.fact: Signed the Kansas-Nebraska Act in 1854.

us-presidents.name: James Buchanan
us-presidents.fact: The only president who never married.

us-presidents.name: Abraham Lincoln
us-presidents.fact: Led the Union during the Civil War and issued the Emancipation Proclamation.

us-presidents.name: Andrew Johnson
us-presidents.party: Democratic; elected vice president on National Union ticket
us-presidents.entry: Succeeded Abraham Lincoln after his assassination.
us-presidents.fact: Congress overrode his veto of Nebraska's statehood law.

us-presidents.name: Ulysses S. Grant
us-presidents.fact: Previously commanded Union armies during the Civil War.

us-presidents.name: Rutherford B. Hayes
us-presidents.entry: Won the disputed 1876 election after an electoral commission process.
us-presidents.fact: His presidency followed the end of the Reconstruction era.

us-presidents.name: James A. Garfield
us-presidents.fact: Assassinated during his first year in office.

us-presidents.name: Chester A. Arthur
us-presidents.entry: Succeeded James Garfield after his death.
us-presidents.fact: Signed the Pendleton Civil Service Reform Act.

us-presidents.name: Grover Cleveland
us-presidents.fact: Later returned for a second, nonconsecutive presidency.

us-presidents.name: Benjamin Harrison
us-presidents.fact: Six states joined the Union during his presidency.

us-presidents.name: Grover Cleveland
us-presidents.entry: Won the 1892 election and returned to office.
us-presidents.fact: Counted as both the twenty-second and twenty-fourth president.

us-presidents.name: William McKinley
us-presidents.fact: President during the Spanish-American War and Hawaii's annexation.

us-presidents.name: Theodore Roosevelt
us-presidents.entry: Succeeded William McKinley after his assassination, then won election in 1904.
us-presidents.fact: The youngest person to become U.S. president.

us-presidents.name: William Howard Taft
us-presidents.fact: Later became Chief Justice of the United States.

us-presidents.name: Woodrow Wilson
us-presidents.fact: President when the United States entered World War I.

us-presidents.name: Warren G. Harding
us-presidents.fact: Died in office in 1923.

us-presidents.name: Calvin Coolidge
us-presidents.entry: Succeeded Warren Harding after his death, then won election in 1924.
us-presidents.fact: His father administered his first presidential oath.

us-presidents.name: Herbert Hoover
us-presidents.fact: The Great Depression began during his presidency.

us-presidents.name: Franklin D. Roosevelt
us-presidents.entry: Won the 1932 presidential election and three reelections.
us-presidents.fact: The only president elected to four terms.

us-presidents.name: Harry S. Truman
us-presidents.entry: Succeeded Franklin Roosevelt after his death, then won election in 1948.
us-presidents.fact: President at the end of World War II and during the Korean War.

us-presidents.name: Dwight D. Eisenhower
us-presidents.fact: Alaska and Hawaii became states during his presidency.

us-presidents.name: John F. Kennedy
us-presidents.fact: The youngest person elected U.S. president.

us-presidents.name: Lyndon B. Johnson
us-presidents.entry: Succeeded John Kennedy after his assassination, then won election in 1964.
us-presidents.fact: Signed the Civil Rights Act of 1964 and Voting Rights Act of 1965.

us-presidents.name: Richard Nixon
us-presidents.fact: The only U.S. president to resign from office.

us-presidents.name: Gerald Ford
us-presidents.entry: Succeeded Richard Nixon after his resignation.
us-presidents.fact: Became both vice president and president without winning a national election for either office.

us-presidents.name: Jimmy Carter
us-presidents.fact: Helped negotiate the Camp David Accords.

us-presidents.name: Ronald Reagan
us-presidents.fact: Previously served as governor of California.

us-presidents.name: George H. W. Bush
us-presidents.fact: President when the Berlin Wall fell in 1989.

us-presidents.name: Bill Clinton
us-presidents.fact: Previously served as governor of Arkansas.

us-presidents.name: George W. Bush
us-presidents.fact: President during the September 11 attacks.

us-presidents.name: Barack Obama
us-presidents.fact: The first African American U.S. president.

us-presidents.name: Donald Trump
us-presidents.fact: Served as the forty-fifth president and later returned as the forty-seventh.

us-presidents.name: Joe Biden
us-presidents.fact: Previously served eight years as vice president.

us-presidents.name: Donald Trump
us-presidents.fact: Returned for a nonconsecutive presidency as the forty-seventh president.

india-pm.name: Jawaharlal Nehru
india-pm.entry: Became prime minister when India became independent.
india-pm.fact: India's first prime minister and longest-serving prime minister.
india-pm.presidentNote: Before 26 January 1950, India had governors-general rather than a republican president: Lord Mountbatten, then C. Rajagopalachari.

india-pm.name: Gulzarilal Nanda
india-pm.entry: Acting prime minister after Nehru's death.
india-pm.fact: Served as acting prime minister on two separate occasions.
india-pm.presidentNote: Includes acting presidents during vacancies where applicable; short temporary delegation of duties is not listed.

india-pm.name: Lal Bahadur Shastri
india-pm.entry: Chosen to lead the government after Nehru.
india-pm.fact: Known for the slogan Jai Jawan, Jai Kisan.
india-pm.presidentNote: Includes acting presidents during vacancies where applicable; short temporary delegation of duties is not listed.

india-pm.name: Gulzarilal Nanda
india-pm.entry: Acting prime minister after Shastri's death.
india-pm.fact: Kept the government running during a second leadership transition.
india-pm.presidentNote: Includes acting presidents during vacancies where applicable; short temporary delegation of duties is not listed.

india-pm.name: Indira Gandhi
india-pm.entry: Chosen as the Congress parliamentary leader and appointed prime minister.
india-pm.fact: India's first woman prime minister; the Emergency occurred during this tenure.
india-pm.presidentNote: Includes acting presidents during vacancies where applicable; short temporary delegation of duties is not listed.

india-pm.name: Morarji Desai
india-pm.entry: Became prime minister after the Janata Party's 1977 election victory.
india-pm.fact: India's first prime minister from outside the Congress party.
india-pm.presidentNote: Includes acting presidents during vacancies where applicable; short temporary delegation of duties is not listed.

india-pm.name: Charan Singh
india-pm.entry: Formed a government after Morarji Desai resigned.
india-pm.fact: Known for his advocacy for farmers.
india-pm.presidentNote: Includes acting presidents during vacancies where applicable; short temporary delegation of duties is not listed.

india-pm.name: Indira Gandhi
india-pm.entry: Returned after Congress won the 1980 general election.
india-pm.fact: Her second continuous tenure ended with her assassination in 1984.
india-pm.presidentNote: Includes acting presidents during vacancies where applicable; short temporary delegation of duties is not listed.

india-pm.name: Rajiv Gandhi
india-pm.entry: Appointed after Indira Gandhi's assassination; later won the 1984 election.
india-pm.fact: At age forty, became India's youngest prime minister.
india-pm.presidentNote: Includes acting presidents during vacancies where applicable; short temporary delegation of duties is not listed.

india-pm.name: V. P. Singh
india-pm.entry: Led the National Front government after the 1989 election.
india-pm.fact: His government implemented the Mandal Commission's reservation recommendations for central government jobs.
india-pm.presidentNote: Includes acting presidents during vacancies where applicable; short temporary delegation of duties is not listed.

india-pm.name: Chandra Shekhar
india-pm.entry: Formed a minority government after V. P. Singh's government fell.
india-pm.fact: His government served during a serious economic crisis.
india-pm.presidentNote: Includes acting presidents during vacancies where applicable; short temporary delegation of duties is not listed.

india-pm.name: P. V. Narasimha Rao
india-pm.entry: Formed the government after the 1991 general election.
india-pm.fact: Major economic liberalisation began under his government in 1991.
india-pm.presidentNote: Includes acting presidents during vacancies where applicable; short temporary delegation of duties is not listed.

india-pm.name: Atal Bihari Vajpayee
india-pm.entry: Invited to form a government after the 1996 election; resigned without a majority.
india-pm.fact: His first government is commonly remembered as the thirteen-day government; he remained caretaker until June 1.
india-pm.presidentNote: Includes acting presidents during vacancies where applicable; short temporary delegation of duties is not listed.

india-pm.name: H. D. Deve Gowda
india-pm.entry: Led the United Front coalition government.
india-pm.fact: Previously served as chief minister of Karnataka.
india-pm.presidentNote: Includes acting presidents during vacancies where applicable; short temporary delegation of duties is not listed.

india-pm.name: I. K. Gujral
india-pm.entry: Succeeded Deve Gowda as leader of the United Front government.
india-pm.fact: Known for the Gujral Doctrine on relations with neighbouring countries.
india-pm.presidentNote: Includes acting presidents during vacancies where applicable; short temporary delegation of duties is not listed.

india-pm.name: Atal Bihari Vajpayee
india-pm.entry: Returned as head of a coalition after the 1998 election and continued after the 1999 election.
india-pm.fact: His government conducted the Pokhran-II nuclear tests in 1998.
india-pm.presidentNote: Includes acting presidents during vacancies where applicable; short temporary delegation of duties is not listed.

india-pm.name: Manmohan Singh
india-pm.entry: Appointed to lead the United Progressive Alliance government.
india-pm.fact: An economist who had earlier served as finance minister during the 1991 reforms.
india-pm.presidentNote: Includes acting presidents during vacancies where applicable; short temporary delegation of duties is not listed.

india-pm.name: Narendra Modi
india-pm.entry: Led the government after the 2014 election and continued after the 2019 and 2024 elections.
india-pm.fact: Began a third consecutive term on 9 June 2024.
india-pm.presidentNote: Includes acting presidents during vacancies where applicable; short temporary delegation of duties is not listed.
